background.text: The age of a child in years cannot be negative.
The number of hours a housekeeping task has been open cannot be negative.
The number of hours a crew member has worked in one shift cannot be negative.
The number of minutes a reserved seat has been unpaid cannot be negative.
The number of crossings completed by the customer in the current calendar year cannot be negative.
The number of passengers in a group booking cannot be negative.
The height of a vehicle in metres cannot be negative.
The number of boarded passengers cannot be negative.
The number of minutes from the film's start cannot be negative.
The number of minutes before departure cannot be negative.
The number of minutes the ship is from the arrival port cannot be negative.

The number of consecutive wrong password entries cannot be negative.

What F8 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger moves a ticket to another sailing and there are no available seats on the new sailing, the ticket must not be changed to the new sailing and a message must be shown to the passenger.
background.formula: (=> (and (and passenger_moves_ticket (not new_sailing_seats_available)) (and ticket_unchanged message_shown)) (and (not ticket_changed) message_shown))

background.text: What F10 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: The requirement applies when a passenger is booking a crossing and the child's age is less than 4 years, in which case the system must issue a ticket.

What F11 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a group booking is paid for and the number of passengers in that booking exceeds 10, then the fare must be reduced by the amount of the group discount code.
What F13 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger enters a discount code that is not valid, the system must display an error message.
What F18 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a vehicle arrives at the check-in lane and its number plate does not match a booking, the driver must be sent to the port office.
What F19 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: Whenever a vehicle is assigned to a boarding lane, the system must print a ticket for the driver.
What F24 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When the loading of the car deck begins, the system must assign vehicles to their boarding lanes in the specific sequence they checked in.

What F27 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a passenger scans an e-ticket at the gate and the ticket is not valid for the next sailing, the system must ensure the gate is not opened and display a message indicating the correct sailing validity.
background.formula: (=> (and (and passenger_scans_e_ticket (not ticket_valid_for_next_sailing)) (and gate_closed valid_sailing_shown)) (and (not gate_opened) message_shown))

background.text: What F30 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When boarding closes and a ticket holder has not boarded, the system must mark the ticket as used (as the only available symbol representing a final ticket state).
What F37 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger enters a door code at a cabin and the entered code is correct, the system must unlock the cabin door.
What F38 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger enters a door code at a cabin and the code is incorrect, the system must ensure the cabin door remains locked.
What F50 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a passenger attempts to pay by bank card and the payment is not approved, the system must cancel the sale and display a message.
What F55 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger orders room service and holds a cabin, the system must ensure the order is sent to the kitchen for delivery.
What F64 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: Whenever a parent registers a child for the kids' club, the system must provide the parent with a pager (indicated by the pager vibrating).

What F65 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When the kids' club calls a parent, the system must ensure the parent's pager vibrates, which is represented by the state where the pager has been given to the parent.

What F70 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: The requirement applies when a passenger with a pet checks in and the pet's vaccination record is not valid, in which case the system must refuse the order (pet) and notify the operations manager (port office).
background.formula: (=> (and (and passenger_checks_in_pet (not vaccination_record_valid)) (and pet_refused port_office_notified)) (and order_refused operations_manager_notified))

background.text: What F76 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a sailing is delayed by more than 120 minutes, the system must provide a meal voucher to each passenger.
What F80 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a customer with an account completes a crossing, the system must add loyalty points for the fare paid.
What F85 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a customer changes their account email address, the system must send a confirmation email to the new address.
What F87 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a customer subscribes to the newsletter, the system must send a confirmation email.
What F88 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a customer unsubscribes from the newsletter, the system must send a confirmation email.
What F89 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: When a crew member registers a found item, the system must record the report.

What F91 demands, in the terms of the other requirements: If a passenger reports a lost item and there is no corresponding found item in the system, the ferry system must record the item description and sailing details.
background.formula: (=> (and (and passenger_reports_lost_item (not matching_found_item_registered)) (and report_recorded reply_sent)) (and item_description_recorded sailing_recorded))

rules.text: WHEN a passenger requests a crossing AND seats are available on the chosen sailing, THE Ferry System SHALL reserve a seat for the passenger.
rules.reading: If a passenger submits a request to book a crossing and there are seats available on the selected sailing, the system must reserve a seat for that passenger.

probes.reading: The system reserves a seat for the passenger only if the passenger requests a crossing and seats are available on the chosen sailing.
If a passenger requests a crossing, the system reserves a seat for the passenger only if seats are available on the chosen sailing.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger requests a crossing AND seats are not available on the chosen sailing, THE Ferry System SHALL offer the next sailing with available seats.
rules.reading: If a passenger requests a crossing and there are no seats available on the chosen sailing, the system must offer the next sailing that has available seats.

probes.reading: The system offers the next sailing with available seats only if a passenger requests a crossing and seats are not available on the chosen sailing.
If a passenger requests a crossing, the system offers the next sailing with available seats only if seats are not available on the chosen sailing.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger pays for a reserved seat, THE Ferry System SHALL send an e-ticket by email.
rules.reading: When a passenger pays for a reserved seat, the system must send an e-ticket by email.

probes.reading: The system sends an e-ticket by email only if the passenger has paid for a reserved seat.

rules.text: WHEN a reserved seat has been unpaid for more than 30 minutes, THE Ferry System SHALL release the seat.
rules.reading: If a reserved seat has remained unpaid for a duration exceeding 30 minutes, the system must release that seat.

alternative.reading: If a reserved seat has remained unpaid for more than 30 minutes, the system must release that seat.

probes.reading: If a reserved seat has remained unpaid for more than 30 minutes, the system must release that seat.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger cancels a ticket more than 24 hours before departure, THE Ferry System SHALL refund the full fare.
rules.reading: If a passenger cancels a ticket and the cancellation occurs more than 24 hours before the departure time, the system must refund the full fare.

If a passenger reports a lost item and no matching found item is registered, the system must record the report, and separately, the system must send a reply within three days.

rules.text: WHEN a found item has been unclaimed for more than 90 days, THE Ferry System SHALL hand the item over to a charity.
rules.reading: If a found item has been unclaimed for more than 90 days, the system must hand the item over to a charity.

probes.reading: The system hands the item over to a charity only if the item has been unclaimed for more than 90 days.
The system hands the item over to a charity if the item has been unclaimed for at least 90 days.
The system hands the item over to a charity if the item has been unclaimed for exactly 90 days.

rules.text: WHEN a crew member presses the man-overboard button, THE Ferry System SHALL sound the alarm on the bridge and record the ship's position.
rules.reading: When a crew member presses the man-overboard button, the system must sound the alarm on the bridge and record the ship's position.

rules.text: WHEN a fire detector raises an alarm, THE Ferry System SHALL show the location of the detector on the bridge panel.
rules.reading: When a fire detector raises an alarm, the system must display the location of that detector on the bridge panel.

probes.reading: The system must display the location of the detector on the bridge panel only if a fire detector has raised an alarm.

rules.text: WHEN a crew member starts a shift, THE Ferry System SHALL record the start time.
rules.reading: Whenever a crew member starts a shift, the system must record the start time.

probes.reading: The system records the start time only if the crew member has started a shift.

rules.text: WHEN a crew member has worked more than 12 hours in one shift, THE Ferry System SHALL alert the chief officer.
rules.reading: The Ferry System must alert the chief officer whenever a crew member's shift duration exceeds 12 hours.

probes.reading: The Ferry System must alert the chief officer whenever a crew member's shift duration is at least 12 hours.
The Ferry System must alert the chief officer whenever a crew member's shift duration is exactly 12 hours.

rules.text: WHEN the ship has docked at the arrival port, THE Ferry System SHALL announce that passengers may leave the ship.
rules.reading: Once the ship has docked at the arrival port, the system must announce that passengers are permitted to leave the ship.

probes.reading: The announcement that passengers may leave the ship is a necessary condition for the ship to be considered docked at the arrival port.
The system must announce that passengers may leave the ship if and only if the ship has docked at the arrival port.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger leaves the ship, THE Ferry System SHALL mark the ticket as used.
rules.reading: Whenever a passenger leaves the ship, the system must mark their ticket as used.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger asks for an invoice, THE Ferry System SHALL email an invoice with the company's tax number.
rules.reading: If a passenger asks for an invoice, the system must email an invoice that includes the company's tax number.

probes.reading: The system emails the invoice only if the passenger has asked for it.
The system emails the invoice if and only if the passenger has asked for it.

rules.text: WHEN a passenger writes a review after the crossing, THE Ferry System SHALL publish the review on the route page.
rules.reading: Whenever a passenger writes a review after a crossing, the system must publish that review on the route page.

probes.reading: The system publishes the review on the route page only if the passenger has written a review after the crossing.

rules.text: THE Ferry System SHALL NOT print tickets.
rules.reading: The system must not print tickets.
